questions.enonce_markdown:
Assess the impact of the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate in Acts 3.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In Acts 3 Peter and John go up to the Temple at the hour of prayer, about three o'clock in the afternoon. A man lame from birth, carried daily to the Beautiful Gate to beg, asks them for money. Peter says, "I have no silver and gold, but I give you what I have; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk" (Acts 3:6). The man leaps up, walks and enters the Temple praising God. This first recorded miracle of the apostles had wide consequences.

**1. Impact on the man himself.** He was healed physically, given a new place in society (he was over forty years old, Acts 4:22), and moved from a beggar at the gate to a worshipper inside the Temple. His healing is a sign of the salvation proclaimed by the apostles.

**2. Impact on the crowd.** The people were filled with wonder and amazement and ran together to Solomon's Portico (Acts 3:10-11). The miracle gave Peter a large audience for his second sermon.

**3. Impact on the preaching of the church.** Peter denies that he has healed by his own power or piety and says that the name of Jesus, and faith in that name, healed the man (Acts 3:12, 16). He proclaims that God has glorified his servant Jesus, whom the people rejected, calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and speaks of the prophet like Moses (Acts 3:13-26). The miracle thus became a sign pointing to Christ.

**4. Impact on the growth of the church.** Many who heard the word believed, and the number of men came to about five thousand (Acts 4:4).

**5. Impact on the relation with the authorities.** The priests, the captain of the Temple and the Sadducees, "greatly annoyed" by the teaching of the resurrection, arrest Peter and John (Acts 4:1-3). Before the Sanhedrin Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, declares that the man was healed in the name of Jesus Christ and that "there is salvation in no one else" (Acts 4:8-12). The council cannot deny the miracle and can only warn the apostles not to speak in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:14-18). The apostles refuse (Acts 4:19-20). The healing thus began the pattern of witness and opposition.

**6. Impact on the faith and courage of the believers.** The community prays for boldness and for further signs and wonders, and the place is shaken and they speak the word of God with boldness (Acts 4:23-31).

**7. Continuity with Jesus.** The miracle recalls the healings of Jesus in Luke and shows that his work continues, now through his name, which agrees with the theme of Luke-Acts.

**Conclusion.** The healing of the lame man was a landmark. It confirmed the apostles' authority, drew the crowds to hear the Gospel, led to many conversions and brought the first official opposition. It shows how, in Acts, deeds and words work together in the spread of the Christian faith.
